angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 28,748,411 km at 214.13 pc = 1.79 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 31940: distance 214.133 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.064), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 214.133 +/- 13.705 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 4.4952 +/- 0.0455 mas (same row, RUWE 1.09), 98.8 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 41.323 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 31940: radius 41.323 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 416.02 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.089) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 28,748,411 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 4058 +/- 125 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 31940: effective temperature 4058 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.045) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 31940: effective temperature 4058 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.045) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, HD 45866: main object type *, Star

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.

surfaceGravitySource: log g 1.61 from 2020AJ....160..120J; the 5 published values span log g 1.475 to 1.812, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.1% of the centre brightness (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020AJ....160..120J)
